lawyer: Shaifuddin Ahmed Choudhury with Khurshed Alam Khan, Advocates ----- For the Petitioner
parties:
Nazrul Islam Majumder (Md) ------ Petitioner
vs
Tahamina Akhtar alias Nahid and another ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Anwarul Haque Choudhury J: This is an application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and is directed against judgment and order dated 12.10.93 passed by the District Judge, Feni dismissing the appeal in Family Miscellaneous Appeal No. 4 of 1993 affirming the order No. 13 dated 31.1.93 allowing the amendment of the plaint under Order 6 rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure in Family Court Case No. 32 of 1992. 

 2. It is the case of the petitioner that he is the defendant No. 1 in Family Court Case No. 32 of 1992, Comilla on 28.11.91 with a prayer for payment of dower money and maintenance for herself and her son and the same was registered as Family Court Case No. 72 of 1991 now remembered 32 of 1992. 

 3. The petitioner as defendant contested the suit by filing written statement and it is pending before the court. When that was the matter the opposite party No. 1 namely the plaintiff preferred Civil Revision before the Hon'ble High Court Division praying for transferring of the Family Court case filed by the present petitioner in the family court of Chittagong asking for restitution of conjugal life to the family court of Comilla from Chittagong. This was ordered and both the cases were allowed to be heard analogously at Feni. Accordingly, both the suits were received in the Family Court, Sadar Feni where it is now pending. The petitioner's case for restitution of conjugal life is now numbered as Family Court Case No. 31 of 1992 and his wife's case renumbered as Family Court Case No. 32 of 1992. 

 4. It is the case of the petitioner's wife that her husband married on 21.2.88 by fixing dower of an amount of Taka 1,00,001.00. One son was born of the wedlock. At the time of marriage the wife was a student of BSc Class of Comilla Mahila College. Her husband maintained all her expenses while she was at Comilla. After some time they were living in Chittagong. The wife went to the house of respondent No. 2 on 24.8.91 to see her ailing father with ornaments and other clothes but she did not turn back. The husband plaintiff served legal notice with a request to come back but the wife would not come. The wife who asked for dower and maintenance subsequently asked for amendment on 5.1.93 contending that her husband did not pay the dower money of Taka 75,000.00 within 28.2.92 as per undertaking dated 28.1.92 executed at her house and that he promised to return the gold ornaments within few days after execution of the undertaking. He failed to comply with the provision of column Nos. 17 and 18 of the registered Kabinnama and as a result on 6.11.92 she divorced her husband, the present petitioner before this court, pronouncing 3 talak by dint of delegated power and as per provision of sections 7 and 8 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance and she supplied a copy thereof to her husband and also gave a notice in writing to the Chairman of the local Union Council of the plaintiff and they acknowledged the receipt of the case. The Family Court allowed the said amendment petition filed by defendant wife vide order No. 13 dated 31.1.93. 

 5. Against that order the present husband petitioner preferred an appeal before the District Judge, Feni in Family Court Case No. 32 of 1992 and the same was registered as Family Miscellaneous Appeal No. 4 of 1993 who upon hearing the parties and perusing the materials on record affirmed the judgment and order of the learned Assistant Judge and dismissed the appeal. Against that this revisional application is moved by the husband who is the defendant in the suit instituted by the wife who filed a suit for maintenance and dower. 

 6. Heard the learned Advocate and perused the application. It appears that in this matter the learned District Judge has disposed of the two Miscellaneous Appeals. 

 7. We have heard the learned Advocate Saifuddin Ahmed Choudhury and perused the application and grounds taken therein. It is the case of the petitioner that both the courts below erred in law in not taking into consideration the facts that the provisions of the Civil Procedure Code is not applicable in Family Court case because those are specifically barred under the provision of section 20 (1) of the Family Court Ordinance which provided "save and as otherwise expressly provided by or under this Ordinance the provisions of the Evidence Act (1 of 1872) and of the Code except sections 10 and 11 shall not apply to proceedings before the Family Courts and as per provision of the section 7 (3) of the said Ordinance only rules 9.10, 11.16, 17.18, 19, 19A, 20, 21, 23, 24, 26, 27, 28 and 29 of Order V of the Code will apply and those are issue of summons and notice". In all others cases the Code of Civil Procedure will not apply but the courts below erred in law in holding that all provisions as under the Civil Procedure Code would apply. There lies the illegality and an error resulting in failure of justice. He has further submitted that this amendment of the plaint as allowed by the court below is also in violation of the law because that will offend the nature and character of the suit and it cannot be done after the written statement has been filed by the husband in Suit No. 32 of 1992. 

 8. We have heard the learned Advocate and examined his submission but we find no substance in those. An amendment of the plaint insofar as it does not change the nature and character of the suit would be allowed always in a suit. In the instant case the amendment was sought for by the wife in her own suit bringing to notice certain facts that accrued or happened after the suit was filed and it is to the effect that she on 6.11.92 divorced her husband by pronouncing 3 (three) talaq by dint of the delegated power and as per provisions of sections 7 and 8 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance and she supplied a copy thereof to her husband and also gave a notice in writing to the Chairman of the local Union Parishad of the plaintiff and they acknowledged the receipt thereof. This is a matter which need, to be taken to the notice of the court and it, in any case, could come to the notice of the court during evidence of the present position. Now if the wife has legally divorced her husband the prayer made by the wife in her plaint that she would be allowed maintenance would be deleted as her maintenance would not be allowed after she had divorced and if the wife had legally divorced the husband, the suit by the husband for restitution of conjugal life may not also be maintainable on that evidence. This, therefore, is a issue vital for both the parties to be decided by the court on evidence and that being the position for ends of justice this amendment needs to be made and it would be incumbent upon the court to do so. In this sort of case the interest of justice needs be served keeping in mind that the other parties should not be taken by surprise by the amendment of the plaint which would change the nature and character of the suit and if justice demands that the amendment should be done it would be within discretion of the court to allow such an amendment for ends of justice. The guiding principle for amendment is that it ought to be made for the purpose of determining the real question in controversy between the parties to any proceeding or for correcting any defect or error in any proceeding. There lies power of the court and the principle applicable to the amendment of the plaint is also applicable to the amendment of the written statement 

 9. In the case of Satish vs. Govt of India AIR 1960 (Cal) 278, the Calcutta High Court reiterated the same principle. It has been again reiterated in the case of Rajesnawar vs Padam, reported in AIR 1970 Raj. 77; AIR 1963 (Madras) 217 (FB) and it is the consistent judicial view that court can take into account subsequent event necessitating amendment by addition of new relief that may be allowed to do complete justice Ref: Kennan vs Chirudu, AIR 1960 Ker. 93). 

 10. In the instant case it is seen that certain facts had happened after the institution of the suit and it is necessary to be taken into notice of the court by way of an amendment for doing complete justice and to settle the real controversy between the parties and in the instant case the court had rightly done so.
